description: Shared serve-credit equivalence-KAT fixture (ARCHIVAL_SERVE_CREDIT_EQUIVALENCE_AUDIT.md section 5). Two legs: the Rust standing KAT (tests/serve_credit_equivalence_kat.rs) asserts verdict AND reason for every vector; the C++ leg (tests/unit_tests/archival_serve_credit_equivalence.cpp) drives the live check_archival_serve_credit_input over every cpp_reachable gate vector via cpp_setup seeded-state mutations and asserts the bool verdict ONLY. The expected_reason column is authored by SOURCE INSPECTION of which MERROR_VER branch each vector trips at substrate_commit -- never extracted from running C++ (section 5 leg-responsibility split). If dev reorders check_archival_serve_credit_input or inserts a predicate, re-author the reason column and bump substrate_commit. The gate base is the gate-2 integration substrate (gate2_serve_credit_kat_v1.json) so the C++ leg reuses its wire + seeding; step-9 expectations reflect the WS-1-corrected as-of-H_fire accessor at the pinned commit (PR #269) on purpose. Re-synced 2026-08-20 to the RF-D1 gate (opaque vin + pruned record): C++-side path bounds retired (now the Rust parser's, via FFI verify), wire round-trip/tag steps retired with the typed vin, leaf index derived (RF-D6).

vectors.note: Green path: the gate-2 integration substrate verbatim.
Step 0 (RF-D1): the opaque vin failed the Rust codec's parse. Rust-only: a blob the C++ serializer guard admits but the codec rejects needs a varint overflow, not worth a C++ setup.
Step 0b (RF-D1): an empty pruned record fails the transport ceiling check before anything is parsed.

Step 1: 65 c1 layers exceeds ARCHIVAL_MAX_PATH_LAYERS_PER_KIND (64). [RF-D1: the path lives in the pruned record; its bounds are the Rust parser's, surfacing as the FFI verify's parse failure rather than a C++ pre-check.]

Step 1: one c1 branch of 257 scalars exceeds ARCHIVAL_MAX_BRANCH_SCALARS (256). [RF-D1: the path lives in the pruned record; its bounds are the Rust parser's, surfacing as the FFI verify's parse failure rather than a C++ pre-check.]

Step 1: one c2 branch of 257 scalars; c1 clean, so the c2 loop reports. [RF-D1: the path lives in the pruned record; its bounds are the Rust parser's, surfacing as the FFI verify's parse failure rather than a C++ pre-check.]

Step 1 ordering fidelity: fat c1 AND fat c2 must report c1 (the C++ loops c1 first). [RF-D1: the path lives in the pruned record; its bounds are the Rust parser's, surfacing as the FFI verify's parse failure rather than a C++ pre-check.]
Step 2 (D-SC-A): (P,42,1) already credited in pre-block LMDB state.
Step 3: no bond record for P.
Step 4: E == join_epoch fails E >= join_epoch + 1 (rejects before any height math is consumed).
Step 5: a bad interval covering E makes good_through false.
Step 6 boundary: current_height == H_close accepts (the C++ compare is strict >).
Step 6 boundary: current_height == H_close + 1 rejects.

Step 6b: current_height == H_seal — the seal block is one past the tip (chain_height is the block count), so it is not yet on chain; the seal-on-chain guard rejects before any block-hash read. Distinct from B-12, which is a read failure at a committed height (corruption).
Step 7: the seal-block hash load throws at a COMMITTED height (current_height > H_seal), i.e. genuine DB corruption — the not-yet-committed case is caught earlier by the seal-on-chain guard (B-11b).
Step 9 (WS-1 slash boundary): holding removed AT h_fire == 19137 -- a slash at at_height means already-removed; rejects.
Step 9 (WS-1 slash boundary): holding removed at h_fire + 1 -- held at fire, gone at tip; the credit is legitimate and accepts (the M2-1 drop-after-serve escape a tip read would re-open).
Step 10: no frozen-segment registry row at H_fire.
Step 11 (RF-D6): the index is DERIVED; a zero registry segment_leaf_count makes the derivation refuse. (Was: wire index == 25992, unrepresentable now.)
Step 12: curve-tree chunk read fails (frozen-segment registry disagrees with the tree).
Step 14: the FFI crypto/path/sig verify rejects (corrupted hybrid signature on the C++ leg).
Empty pre-block set: (P,42,1) is not a duplicate. Pins the BE key bytes (shekyl_types.h ArchivalServeCreditKey).
Pre-block set holds (P,42,1): duplicate.
Set holds (P,42,1); probe (P,1,42) -- field-swapped triple must not collide.

Distinct triples across two personas: unique. Pins the first triple's ArchivalServeCreditKey big-endian bytes -- post-SCE-1-unify the blockchain.cpp block pass and the D-SC-A persistent key share this one encoding (audit doc section 6).
(P,42,1) recurs at indices 2 and 4; the C++ rejects on the FIRST insert failure (index 2).
(shard,E) = (1,42) vs (42,1): distinct keys, no collision.

sce1_crosscheck.note: SCE-1 (audit doc section 6) -- RESOLVED by the post-equivalence unify commit: the block-level D-SC-C pass now keys with ArchivalServeCreditKey, the same big-endian encoding D-SC-A persists (db_lmdb.cpp:1657-1659 forbids native-endian composite keys). This cross-check pins both decision paths to the one encoding; expect_equal is now true and load-bearing -- a reintroduced split fails both legs here. Equivalence was proven against the pre-unify native-endian bytes first (mirror-then-fix); the decision-invariance fuzz target holds the encoding-independence property standing.
